briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Bets on a Tax Fix While DEA Inches Toward Schedule III
briefs.top: Michigan operators are getting real ammunition this fall: bipartisan repeal bills are moving on the 24% wholesale tax and Detroit brands just swept the city's top cannabis awards. Nationally, the DEA's own lawyers now argue marijuana doesn't belong in Schedule I anymore, while the FDA is fast-tracking psilocybin and MDMA therapies toward approval.

local.text: Detroit dispensaries sweep Metro Times' Best of Detroit — The Refinery, Hytek and sister brand Growing Pains combined for six wins across staff and reader-voted categories, with Growing Pains praised for building from a basement operation into one of the state's most respected names.

Muskegon dispensary-restaurant hybrid targets fall opening — Fields Cannary is pushing the retail format further than most Michigan shops, pairing a cannabis dispensary with a full-service restaurant as it eyes a fall launch.

JARS Cannabis forces removal of controversial Flock camera — Madison Heights took down the license-plate camera aimed at the dispensary's lot after a public 'No Flock Zone' standoff, with JARS saying it acted on customer privacy concerns.

Bipartisan bills to scrap the 24% wholesale tax gain traction — Rep. James DeSana's HB 6224 mirrors a Senate repeal bill backed by both Republicans and Democrats, arguing the levy is badly underperforming and hurting licensed operators' ability to compete with the illicit market.

Tax fight heads to the Court of Appeals as retail base holds — MiCIA is pressing its unconstitutionality claim after a Court of Claims loss, and while active retail licenses slipped only slightly, from 845 to 836 over the year, operators are betting relief is still on the table.

national.text: DEA's own brief argues weed no longer fits Schedule I — After an 11-day administrative hearing wrapped in July and final briefs landed in August, the agency itself now contends marijuana no longer meets the statutory criteria for Schedule I, leaving only the judge's recommendation before a formal order.

FDA fast-tracks three psychedelic therapies to market — Compass Pathways, Usona Institute and Transcend Therapeutics each landed a National Priority Voucher in April, compressing FDA review from roughly ten to twelve months down to just one or two.

Compass Pathways builds provider pipeline ahead of approval — The company tapped training firm Fluence to design post-approval clinician programs for COMP360 psilocybin therapy, a concrete signal it's preparing for a possible market launch.

Curaleaf's $1.5B+ Aurora takeover bid moves forward — Curaleaf formally commenced its tender offer for Aurora Cannabis at a 45% premium, a cross-border consolidation move the industry is watching as a template for future MSO deals.

States still waiting on DEA rescheduling guidance — California's cannabis regulator says the DEA has shown 'any sort of interest' in helping states implement the rescheduling move, even as it simultaneously seeks more information from California's medical program.
